description: Workload-bound principal in AWS IAM, Azure managed identity, or GCP service account used by compute resources to call cloud APIs
typical_secrets: STS tokens; managed-identity tokens; metadata-server tokens; SA JSON keys (legacy)

description: Pod-bound identity issued by the K8s API server, projected as a short-lived JWT via TokenRequest API
typical_secrets: Projected SA tokens (audience-bound JWTs); legacy long-lived SA tokens

description: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, CircleCI job identity; increasingly OIDC-federated to cloud IAM
typical_secrets: OIDC ID tokens; repo/org secrets; deploy keys; PATs

description: Registry credential used by orchestrators and build tools to pull container images
typical_secrets: OAuth2 tokens; docker-config JSON; robot accounts

description: Application-to-database principal (RDBMS, NoSQL, warehouse) for reads and writes
typical_secrets: Username/password; client certs; IAM-DB tokens (RDS IAM, Cloud SQL IAM)

description: X.509 identity for a web/API workload (server TLS) or mTLS workload-to-workload identity (e.g., SPIFFE/SPIRE)
typical_secrets: X.509 certificates + private keys; SPIFFE SVIDs (X.509-SVID, JWT-SVID)

short_name: Third-party SaaS API key / OAuth client
description: OAuth client credential or static API key used to call an external SaaS (Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Datadog)
typical_secrets: OAuth client_id+secret; refresh tokens; static API keys; webhook signing secrets

description: Source-control identity (PAT, SSH key, deploy key, GitHub App) used by humans, bots and pipelines
typical_secrets: Personal Access Tokens; fine-grained tokens; SSH keys; deploy keys; GitHub App installation tokens

description: Ansible AAP, Puppet, Chef, Terraform Cloud/Enterprise, Pulumi agents on build farms and ephemeral runners
typical_secrets: Tower/AAP creds; Vault AppRoles; TFC team tokens; dynamic cloud creds

description: Datadog, Splunk forwarders, Dynatrace OneAgent, Prometheus exporters, Elastic Beats, New Relic agents on hosts and containers
typical_secrets: API keys; ingest tokens; mTLS certs

description: Producer/consumer for Kafka, RabbitMQ, Pulsar, SQS/SNS, Service Bus, Pub/Sub, Event Grid
typical_secrets: SASL/SCRAM creds; mTLS certs; IAM signed requests; shared-access signatures (SAS)

description: On-prem and hybrid domain service accounts (svc_-prefixed) for Windows file/print, SQL Server, SharePoint, Exchange hybrid
typical_secrets: Passwords (often static); Kerberos keys; gMSA / sMSA; msDS-KeyCredentialLink

description: Identity an API gateway (Apigee, Kong, AWS API GW, Azure APIM, F5, NGINX+) presents to upstream services
typical_secrets: mTLS client certs; signed JWTs; HMAC keys; AWS SigV4 IAM creds

description: UiPath, Blue Prism, Automation Anywhere robot identity; frequently authenticated as a real AD user
typical_secrets: AD user passwords vaulted in Orchestrator; MFA bypass tokens; browser session cookies

description: Identity that signs binaries, container images, packages, SBOM attestations; ephemeral (Sigstore) or hardware-backed (Authenticode, Apple Notary)
typical_secrets: Fulcio short-lived certs; EV/OV code-signing certs in HSM; Apple Developer ID keys; GPG package-repo keys

description: Identity that signs in-toto / SLSA provenance statements proving how an artifact was built
typical_secrets: Sigstore keyless OIDC creds; TUF root keys; in-toto layout keys

description: Identity the mesh control plane (Istiod, Linkerd identity, Consul Connect CA) uses to mint workload SVIDs
typical_secrets: Intermediate-CA private keys; bootstrap tokens; root-CA trust bundles

description: Identity rooted in a TEE (SGX/TDX, SEV-SNP, Nitro Enclaves, Azure CVMs, Confidential Space) attesting measurements before secret release
typical_secrets: Attestation reports/quotes; ephemeral RSA keys bound to measurement; MAA / Nitro attestation documents

description: LLM-driven agent (LangChain, AutoGen, Copilot Studio, Agentforce, custom agentic frameworks) calling tools, APIs and human-facing systems
typical_secrets: OAuth on-behalf-of tokens; static tool API keys; retrieval-store creds; model-provider keys; vector-DB tokens

description: Identity that pushes/pulls trained models from MLflow, SageMaker Model Registry, Hugging Face, Vertex Model Garden, Azure ML
typical_secrets: Registry tokens; S3/GCS/Blob credentials; signed model artifacts

description: Per-device identity for sensors, gateways, ATMs, POS terminals, branch printers, BMS, EV chargers; often hardware-rooted (TPM, SE)
typical_secrets: Per-device X.509; DPS-issued certs; TPM-attested keys; symmetric PSKs (legacy)

description: RACF/ACF2/Top Secret userIDs for started tasks, CICS region IDs, IMS dep-region IDs, batch scheduler IDs; AS/400 profiles
typical_secrets: RACF passphrases; IBM MFA tokens; certs in RACF keyrings; ICSF master keys

description: The non-human KMS/HSM custodian PRINCIPAL that controls TDE/CMK master keys for SQL Server, Oracle TDE, PG pgcrypto, AlwaysEncrypted, MongoDB CSFLE. NOTE: the master key itself is a managed SECRET, not an identity (NIST NPE / OWASP) — this row is the controlling principal, not the key
typical_secrets: KMS CMK ARN + KMS policy; HSM partition credential; Always Encrypted CMK in Azure KV

short_name: HSM/KMS operator (HUMAN-privileged — out of NHI scope)
description: Privileged HUMAN operators administering HSM (CloudHSM, Thales Luna, nShield, Entrust, Utimaco) or KMS control plane under M-of-N quorum. Reclassified as a HUMAN identity per NIST NPE ('not a human actor'); the non-human KMS auto-unseal principal is NHI-035. Retained as a row for FK traceability; governed via UC-N-010
typical_secrets: PED keys; smartcards; Shamir quorum shares; CloudHSM CO/CU/AU principals

short_name: Private-CA operator roles (HUMAN — out of NHI scope)
description: Privileged HUMAN PKI roles in private CA (ADCS, EJBCA, Venafi TPP/TLSPC, Keyfactor Command, AWS Private CA, GCP CAS): RA, CA admin, auditor, enrolment agent. Reclassified HUMAN per NIST NPE; the non-human issuing-CA SIGNING identity is the true NHI (mesh CA = NHI-017). Retained for FK traceability; governed via UC-N-010
typical_secrets: Smartcard-bound admin certs; enrolment-agent certs; CA private keys in HSM; ACME EAB keys

description: NetBackup, Commvault, Veeam, Rubrik, Cohesity, Druva agent identities with cross-system read access; prime ransomware target
typical_secrets: Privileged AD service accounts; hypervisor admin creds; immutable-storage tokens (object-lock)

description: Service identities that exchange user tokens for downstream-API tokens (OAuth 2.0 token exchange, OBO flow, JWT bearer grant)
typical_secrets: Confidential-client secrets; signed JWT assertions (private_key_jwt); DPoP keys

short_name: Federated B2B / Open Banking client identity
description: mTLS / FAPI 2.0 client identities for partner banks, fintechs and Australian Consumer Data Right (CDR) data recipients
typical_secrets: mTLS client certs (FAPI 2.0); software-statement assertions (SSAs); DPoP keys

description: A non-human service account (oracle, sapadm, weblogic, svc_batch, shared Tableau/Power BI) whose RISK is concurrent use by multiple humans AND scripts — the OWASP NHI10:2025 'Human Use of NHI' anti-pattern. Common in legacy ops and outsourced run teams
typical_secrets: Long passwords; SSH keys on shared filesystems; RDP saved credentials

short_name: Browser / SaaS extension and OAuth-app identity
description: Third-party app installed into Google Workspace, M365, Salesforce, Slack, GitHub Apps; operating with delegated scopes on tenant data
typical_secrets: OAuth refresh tokens (long-lived); app-installation tokens; webhook secrets; marketplace API keys

description: Inbound caller identity asserted via HMAC-signed webhooks, mTLS or replay-protected JWTs (Stripe, GitHub, Twilio, payment gateways)
typical_secrets: HMAC signing secrets; webhook endpoint secrets; JWKs

description: Router, switch, firewall, load-balancer, SD-WAN edge identities used by NetOps automation and TACACS+/RADIUS principals
typical_secrets: SSH keys; TACACS+ shared secrets; SNMPv3 creds; vendor cloud-controller tokens (Meraki, Panorama, Aruba Central)

description: Network printer, MFP, cheque scanner, ATM peripheral, kiosk identities; historically authenticated via default credentials
typical_secrets: SNMPv3 creds; 802.1X EAP-TLS certs; default admin creds

description: NOT a distinct identity — a CROSS-CUTTING crypto-migration attribute of existing PKI identities (NHI-006, NHI-017, NHI-025) during PQC (NIST FIPS 203/204/205) and hybrid-cert rollouts: dual-signed certs, PQC-capable CAs and HSMs. Dual-signed certs are credentials, not actors. Tracked via UC-N-013
typical_secrets: Hybrid X.509 (classical + PQC); ML-DSA private keys; composite signatures

description: The vault's own identities: auto-unseal KMS principals, replication tokens, DR replication identities, agent / proxy / gateway identities
typical_secrets: Root tokens; Shamir recovery keys; Sentinel policy admin tokens; auto-unseal KMS keys

short_name: Ephemeral workload via SPIFFE / Aembit / Clutch
description: Zero-trust workload identity issued just-in-time after attestation (kernel, K8s, AWS metadata); replaces static secrets
typical_secrets: Short-lived JWTs; X.509-SVIDs; signed-attestation-bound tokens

description: Decommissioned-app service accounts still active, expired-team credentials, test accounts in production, ex-vendor back-doors
typical_secrets: Anything; rarely rotated
